rationale: Both miss all four concrete, reproduced bugs the human reviewer pinpointed (max_num_seqs default crash, dropped revision/seed/download_dir fields, model_subdir/tokenizer_subdir fallback loss, omni_kv_config precedence flip), so recall is low for both. Y engages more substantively with the reviewer's top-level architectural worry (wrong owner sets, parity tests blind to drift) via its own well-reproduced findings — ownership validation rejecting ~226 legitimate args, a scheduler_cls divergence swept across 51 pipelines, and a demonstrated parity-test blind spot — backed by actually running the suite and tracing call sites. X is comparably well-grounded and cites precise evidence, but its findings are narrower/more scattered across many minor claim-verified bullets and connect less directly to what the human reviewer actually flagged.
